adults.title: Many Heartfelt I Knows
adults.big_idea: A testimony of Jesus Christ is a personal gift from God, and He gives it to us to be shared, simply and with love.
adults.objective: Learners will put their own witness of the Savior into one or two simple, true sentences and choose a person and a setting in which to share it this week.
prepare: Read Elder Caussé’s talk, especially paragraphs T03.13–T03.22 and T03.26–T03.31.
Bring a slip of paper and a pen for each person.
Write on the board before class: Why me? and, beneath it, a blank line.
Pray for one or two class members by name who may feel their testimony is too small to share.

segments.name: A better question
steps: Begin with prayer. Point to the board and explain that Elder Caussé said he often wondered why he was so privileged to receive a testimony, and never found a fully satisfying answer.
Tell the class that over time he came to ask a better question. Write it on the blank line: “What does the Lord expect me to do with this gift?”
Give everyone thirty seconds of silence with that question before anyone speaks.
questions: How does the second question change what you feel responsible for?

segments.name: A gift that is uniquely yours
steps: Ask someone to read paragraph T03.13 aloud while the class listens for how a testimony is received and how it grows. List what they heard on the board (faith, earnest seeking, gospel living, the quiet influence of the Holy Ghost).
Have the class turn to Doctrine and Covenants 46:13 and read it silently, then name the gift described there.
Read the invitation in T03.14: “Please trust it, nurture it, and bear it, because it is uniquely yours.” Circle the three verbs on the board: trust, nurture, bear.
Pair-share for two minutes using the questions below.
questions: Which of the three is hardest for you right now: to trust your testimony, to nurture it, or to bear it? Why?
When have you been tempted to measure your testimony against someone else’s?

segments.name: I know and I love you
steps: Divide into groups of three or four. Ask each group to read paragraphs T03.17–T03.20 together and mark every connection Elder Caussé makes between testimony and love.
Ask each group to report one connection. Make sure both directions come out: saying “I know” is an expression of love, and saying “I love you” sincerely is a way of bearing witness of the Savior.
Read the aligned quote from Elder Gilbert and ask how it fits what the groups found.
Point out the promise in T03.20: when these expressions of faith and love come together, they help create an environment where the Spirit of the Lord can dwell and bring joy.
questions: Whose simple “I know” has stayed with you for years? What made it reach you?
In your home or among your friends, which is said less often: I know or I love you? What would change if both were heard more?

segments.name: The Almas around us
steps: Read Alma 36:17 together. Ask what Alma remembered in his moment of anguish, and from whom he had heard it.
Read paragraphs T03.28–T03.29. Note that Elder Caussé calls that remembered witness a spark of hope.

Invite everyone to think silently of one person who may be waiting to discover, or rediscover, hope in Jesus Christ. Ask them to write that person’s first name or initials on their slip of paper. No one will be asked to share the name.
Read the first aligned quote, the Prophet Joseph Smith’s statement that Elder Caussé cites, and then T03.10. Ask how the witness of apostles and the witness of every member work together.
questions: Alma’s father could not have known when his words would be remembered. What does that suggest about a testimony we share that seems to go unheard?

segments.name: Short, sincere and true
steps: Briefly retell the story of Elder Caussé’s niece in T03.21: at a Young Women camp she was so nervous she managed only two simple sentences, felt discouraged afterward, and her mother asked, “Do you believe what you said?”
Read T03.22 aloud. Ask the class for the three things a testimony need not be and the one thing it needs to be.

Silent writing, two minutes: on the back of the slip, each person writes one or two sentences of witness they truly believe, in words they would naturally use. Elder Caussé’s examples in T03.31 can serve as models.

Invite everyone to turn to a neighbor and say their sentences aloud once. Anyone who prefers may simply read them silently. This is the check for understanding: every person leaves having put a witness into words.

segments.name: Look each day
steps: Read the invitation from T03.31 in the invitations list, and then the promise in T03.27: as we share our testimony freely it will grow stronger, we will draw closer to the Lord, and we will become instruments in His hands.

Ask each person to write on the slip one setting from Elder Caussé’s list (home, testimony meeting, a ministering visit, social media, an everyday conversation) where they will share their sentences this week with the person they named.
Tell the class that next week you will begin by asking two or three people what happened when they looked for an opportunity. Close with your own brief witness of the Savior.

key_quotes.text: Our testimony is not a talent to be hidden. It is a gift to be shared—with grateful hearts and in a spirit of humility and love.
To say “I know” is a tender expression of love toward our neighbor.
It need not be long, eloquent, or dramatic—it only needs to be true.
How many “Almas” are there around you waiting to hear your witness and discover, or rediscover, the hope that is found in Jesus Christ?

scriptures.use: Read silently in the second segment; ask the class to name the gift described and connect it to Elder Caussé’s phrase about a precious gift from God.
Read aloud in the fourth segment; ask what Alma remembered in his anguish and who had borne that witness to him.
For home study or if time allows: read and ask how sharing our witness helps us keep the covenant to take upon ourselves the name of Christ (see T03.12).

aligned_quotes.speaker: The Prophet Joseph Smith
aligned_quotes.text: The fundamental principles of our religion are the testimony of the Apostles and Prophets, concerning Jesus Christ.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Gilbert
aligned_quotes.text: For disciples of Jesus Christ, truth and love always walk together.

invitations.text: I invite you to look each day for opportunities, as prompted by the Holy Ghost, to bear witness of Jesus Christ and His restored gospel
Please trust it, nurture it, and bear it, because it is uniquely yours.

takeaways: My testimony is a personal gift from God, and it is uniquely mine.
A testimony does not need to be long or eloquent; it only needs to be true.
Sharing what I know is a way of loving people, and loving people is a way of bearing witness of Christ.
act: Each morning this week, pray to notice one opportunity to bear witness of the Savior, even for a minute or two.
Share the one or two sentences you wrote with the person whose name is on your slip, in the setting you chose.
At home, pair one sincere I know with one sincere I love you in the same conversation.
Write down what happened and how you felt, and come ready to tell the class next week.
music: I Know That My Redeemer Lives
adapt: At home with two or three adults: skip the groups, read T03.17–T03.20 aloud together, and let each person finish the sentence I know… and the sentence I love… for the others in the room.
Large class: keep the pair-shares and take only two reports from each discussion so that the writing segment is not cut.
Only fifteen minutes: teach the first, fifth and sixth segments.

youth.title: Two True Sentences
youth.big_idea: You do not need a perfect or impressive testimony to share it; a short, sincere witness of Jesus Christ carries power because the Holy Ghost confirms it.
youth.objective: Youth will write a testimony of two true sentences in their own words and choose one real moment this week to share it.
prepare: Read Elder Caussé’s talk, especially T03.14, T03.21–T03.23 and T03.30–T03.31.
Bring an index card or slip of paper and a pen for each person.
Ask youth to bring scriptures or have the Gospel Library app open to Doctrine and Covenants 100.
Write on the board: Long. Eloquent. Dramatic. True.

segments.name: Sixty seconds
steps: As soon as the prayer ends, hand out the cards and say: You have sixty seconds. Write two things you honestly believe about God or Jesus Christ. Two sentences only. No one will collect these.
When time is up, ask them to turn the cards face down and keep them.
Ask for a show of hands on the questions below. Be honest about your own answer.
questions: Who found that harder than expected?
Who has ever stayed in their seat in a testimony meeting because they thought what they had to say was not enough?

segments.name: The girl at camp
steps: Ask a confident reader to read T03.21, the experience Elder Caussé’s niece shared from her youth.
Ask the group to retell it in order: where she was, how many sentences she managed, how she felt in the days afterward, and what her mother asked her.
Write her mother’s question on the board: “Do you believe what you said?”
Point to the four words on the board. Read T03.22 and ask a youth to cross out the three words a testimony does not need to be and circle the one it does.
questions: Why do we compare our testimonies with other people’s? What does comparing do to us?
If a friend told you they felt the way she did after camp, what would you say?

segments.name: Where the power comes from
steps: Divide into two teams. Team one reads Doctrine and Covenants 100:5–8. Team two reads T03.23–T03.25. Each team has two minutes to find the answer to this question: If my words are simple, why would they matter to anyone?

Each team sends one person to the board to write its answer in ten words or fewer. Let the group decide which answer says it most clearly, then read T03.23 to confirm that it is the Spirit, not words, that testifies of the truth.
Read the aligned quote from Elder Stevenson and ask which of his three words is the easiest starting point for them.

Answer the honest question many youth carry. Read T03.30 and point out the phrase about a testimony that is only the beginning of one, and T03.14, where Elder Caussé says our testimonies may differ from those of family members or fellow Saints.
questions: What can you honestly say right now, even if you would not yet say I know about everything?

segments.name: I know and I love you
steps: Ask a youth to read T03.18–T03.19. Ask what Elder Caussé says the words “I know” express, and what a sincere “I love you” does.

In pairs, give two minutes to list as many real places as they can where a youth could share a one-line belief naturally. Start them with Elder Caussé’s own list in T03.31: home, testimony meeting, ministering, social media, everyday interactions. The pair with the longest realistic list reads it aloud.
Role play, two minutes: in the same pairs, one person plays a friend who asks, Why do you go to church every week? The other answers in one or two honest sentences. Switch.
Briefly tell how Alma, at his lowest moment, remembered his father’s witness of Jesus Christ (Alma 36:17). Ask them to think silently of one person their age who might need a spark of hope like that.
questions: What makes sharing a belief feel natural instead of awkward or preachy?

segments.name: Write it for real
steps: Ask everyone to turn their card over and reread their two sentences from the start of class. Ask the niece’s mother’s question: Do you believe what you wrote?
Give three minutes of quiet to rewrite the two sentences on the other side, in the words they would actually use. Show Elder Caussé’s two examples from T03.31 as models of how simple it can be.

Invite them to take out their phones and type their sentences into a note, or into a draft message to one person they thought of. They decide later whether and when to send it; no one should feel pushed to post anything.
Invite two or three volunteers to read their sentences aloud. Thank each one without commenting on wording. This is your check for understanding.

segments.name: The one-week challenge
steps: Read the invitation from T03.31 in the invitations list. Stress the words each day and prompted by the Holy Ghost.
Read the promise in T03.27: as they share freely, their own testimony will grow stronger and they will draw closer to the Lord.

Challenge: share your two sentences with one person this week, out loud or in writing, and say one sincere I love you at home. Ask them to write the person’s initials on the card and keep it in their scriptures or phone case.
Tell them you will start next week by asking who did it and what happened, and that you will report on your own attempt first. Close with your two sentences.

key_quotes.text: It need not be long, eloquent, or dramatic—it only needs to be true.
Your testimony may be different from mine or that of other family members or fellow Saints. Please trust it, nurture it, and bear it, because it is uniquely yours.
If you have received the gift of a testimony—even if it is only the beginning of one—it is your duty and privilege to share it.
do you realize that your testimony can literally change lives—your own and the lives of others?

scriptures.use: Team one reads it in the third segment and reports, in ten words or fewer, what the Lord promises to do when we speak by the power of the Holy Ghost.
Refer to it in the fourth segment; a youth may read it aloud. Ask whose witness Alma remembered and what it led him to do.
Optional closing: read it as the promise that brought Elder Caussé peace when he was called (T03.02). Ask which phrase would help a nervous person stand up.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Stevenson
aligned_quotes.text: I invite you to do something that is as simple as gospel fruit is delicious: love, share, and invite.

invitations.text: I invite you to look each day for opportunities, as prompted by the Holy Ghost, to bear witness of Jesus Christ and His restored gospel
Please trust it, nurture it, and bear it, because it is uniquely yours.

takeaways: My testimony does not have to sound like anyone else’s; it only needs to be true.
The Holy Ghost, not my wording, carries a testimony to another person’s heart.
Even the beginning of a testimony is a gift worth sharing.
act: Share your two sentences with one person this week, out loud, in a note or in a message.
Pray each morning to notice one moment when the Holy Ghost prompts you to say what you believe.
Say one sincere I love you to someone at home and notice how it changes the feeling there.
Keep your card where you will see it and add a third sentence when you find you believe one more thing.
music: I Know That My Redeemer Lives
adapt: At home with one or two youth: do the sixty-second card together with a parent writing too, read T03.21–T03.22, and share your sentences with each other at the end.
Large class: run the team activity in four teams, two on each reading, and take only one volunteer per team in the writing segment.
Short on time: keep the first, second, fifth and sixth segments.

children.title: My Testimony Is a Gift to Share
children.big_idea: Heavenly Father gives me a testimony of Jesus Christ, and I can share it with simple, true words.
children.objective: Each child will say one true sentence about Heavenly Father or Jesus Christ and choose someone to share it with this week.
prepare: Read T03.16 and T03.21–T03.22 in Elder Caussé’s talk.
Bring a flashlight, a small blanket or towel, and a soft ball.
Bring a small box or bag wrapped or tied like a present, with a picture of the Savior inside.
Bring paper and crayons for each child.

segments.name: What is in the gift?
steps: After the prayer, hold up the wrapped box. Ask the children what they like to do when they are given a present.
Let a child open it and show the picture of the Savior to everyone.
Explain that Elder Caussé, one of the Lord’s Apostles, taught that knowing Jesus Christ is the Son of God is a precious gift from Heavenly Father. That gift is called a testimony.
Teach the sentence for today and say it together twice: My testimony is a gift to share.
questions: What do you know about Jesus?

segments.name: Hidden light, shared light
steps: Dim the lights if you can. Turn on the flashlight and put it under the blanket. Ask who the light can help now.
Let a child pull the blanket off and shine the light on the picture of the Savior. Ask what changed.
Tell the children that Elder Caussé said a testimony is not something to be hidden; it is a gift to be shared.
Movement: when you cover the flashlight, the children crouch down small and quiet. When you uncover it, they stand tall and say, I can share. Repeat four or five times, getting quicker.
questions: How do we share a testimony? (We say what we know is true, and we show love.)

segments.name: The girl who said two sentences
steps: Tell the story simply: Elder Caussé’s niece went to a camp with other young women. She stood up to share her testimony. She felt so nervous that she said only two short sentences.

Hold up one finger and say her first sentence: “I know that God loves me.” Hold up two fingers and say her second: “I know that God has a plan for me.” Have the children repeat both with their fingers.

Continue: afterward she felt sad because she wished she could speak like the other girls. Her mother asked whether she believed what she had said. She said yes. Her mother told her that was all that mattered.
Act it out: one child plays the niece and says the two sentences; another plays the mother and asks, Do you believe it? The class answers together, Yes. Repeat with new actors.
questions: Does a testimony have to be long?
What does a testimony need to be? (True.)

segments.name: I know ball
steps: Sit in a circle. Explain that Elder Caussé said the Holy Ghost helps people feel that our words are true, even when our words are simple.

Roll or gently toss the ball to a child. That child finishes the sentence I know… with something true about Heavenly Father or Jesus, then passes the ball on. Offer starters if needed: I know Jesus loves me. I know Heavenly Father hears my prayers.
A child may repeat what another child said or pass with a smile. After each one, the class whispers, That is true.
Go around until every child who wants a turn has had one. This is how you will know each child can say a simple testimony.

segments.name: Sing what we know
steps: Sing I Know My Father Lives. Ask the children to put a hand on their heart each time they sing the words I know.
Tell them Elder Caussé taught that saying I love you with a kind and honest heart is also a way to share a testimony of Jesus, because all perfect love comes from Him.
Stand and practice: turn to a neighbor and say, Jesus loves you. Then sing the song once more, or sing Jesus Said Love Everyone.

segments.name: Draw my testimony
steps: Give each child paper and crayons. Ask them to draw one thing they know is true about Heavenly Father or Jesus.
As they draw, move around and help each child write, or write for them, one I know sentence at the bottom of the page.
Ask each child to think of one person they could show the picture to and tell their sentence. Keep it open: someone at home, a grandparent, a friend, a neighbor, a teacher.
questions: Who will you share your picture with?

segments.name: Share it this week
steps: Hold up the flashlight one more time and say the sentence together: My testimony is a gift to share.
Tell the children that Elder Caussé invited everyone to look each day for a chance to share what they believe about Jesus, and he taught that when we share our testimony it grows stronger.
Invite each child to share their picture and sentence with the person they chose. Tell them that next week you will ask who they shared with.
Share your own testimony in two short sentences and close with prayer.

key_quotes.text: Our testimony is not a talent to be hidden. It is a gift to be shared
It need not be long, eloquent, or dramatic—it only needs to be true.
I love our Savior, Jesus Christ

scriptures.use: With older children, read the verse aloud and ask them to listen for the word witnesses; explain that a witness tells what he or she knows is true.
Tell the children that this verse helped Elder Caussé feel peace; have an older child read it and ask what the Lord says to do instead of being afraid.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Fale
aligned_quotes.text: I am a child of God and He loves me.

invitations.text: I invite you to look each day for opportunities, as prompted by the Holy Ghost, to bear witness of Jesus Christ and His restored gospel

takeaways: My testimony is a gift from Heavenly Father.
My testimony can be short if it is true.
I can share what I know about Jesus and show love.
act: Show your picture to the person you chose and tell them your I know sentence.
Say I love you to someone this week and remember that love comes from Jesus.
When you pray, thank Heavenly Father for one thing you know is true.

adapt.younger: Ages 3–7: shorten the story to three sentences and let every child hold up one and two fingers for the niece’s two sentences. Repeat the flashlight crouch-and-stand game between activities whenever attention drifts. In the ball game, say a sentence for the child to echo, such as I know Jesus loves me, and roll the ball instead of tossing it. Let a helper write each child’s sentence on the drawing.
adapt.older: Ages 8–11: have a child read Mosiah 18:9 aloud and another read Elder Fale’s sentence in the aligned quote as an example of a short testimony. Ask the harder question: Why might a short testimony reach someone’s heart as well as a long one? Let an older child lead the ball game and another play the mother in the story. Invite them to write two I know sentences of their own on their drawing.
